# The Cost of Intelligence, Episode 21: Same Price Per Token, a 5x Bigger Bill


### Fable 5.2 and GPT-6.2 Astra charge the same per token. One test’s bill was 5x bigger. Plus Jensen’s return, server re-quotes, the Dec 1 cliff, and three cost cuts.


[Strong Compute](https://substack.com/@strongcompute)


Nov 24, 2026


*Listen to this episode on [Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/episode/1BXHEgGHWr2pbMHb6pDdLb) or watch it on [YouTube](https://youtu.be/9bygYacMjmM) .*


Welcome back to


**The Cost of Intelligence** , our comedy news show about the money behind AI. Each episode, Ben Sand reads the industry’s invoice and asks one question: are you getting more intelligence per dollar?


This week:


**Triple Header Tuesday** runs tokens per dollar, the subscription Tier List and tasks per dollar.


**Nvidia’s board brings back Jensen Huang** , and the market rips.


**AI server makers** want more money on orders already signed. The


**December 1 price cliff** , in ten-dollar bills.


**Vercel** wants receipts. Plus three cuts from the Department of Token Efficiency. Here’s the written version, with every source linked.


---


## Triple Header Tuesday


Today’s unit is ten dollars of output tokens, at list prices. More tokens, better deal.


**Out in front, a three-way tie at 20 million tokens:** Claude Haiku 5.5 at $0.50 per million output tokens, on prompts under 100,000 tokens (


[Anthropic](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing) ); OpenAI’s GPT-6 Luna at $0.50 (


[OpenAI](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing) ); and Thinking Machines’ Inkling 2 Mini on its own Tinker service at $0.50 (


[Tinker](https://thinkingmachines.ai/tinker/pricing/) ). On OpenRouter, one Inkling 2 Mini provider charges $0.30, about


**33 million** tokens for ten dollars, and the cheapest listing there is lower still (


[OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai/thinkingmachines/inkling-2-mini) ).


**DeepSeek V4.1 Flash** on DeepSeek’s own API: $1.20 at peak, about


**8.3 million** tokens; off-peak, $0.60, about


**16.7 million** (


[DeepSeek](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing) ). OpenRouter’s cheapest provider lists it at about $0.20, around


**50 million** (


[OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash) ).


**The middle of the pack:** Mistral Large 4 on Mistral’s API at $2.10, about


**4.8 million** (


[Mistral](https://docs.mistral.ai/models/mistral-large-4-0) ); DeepSeek V4 Pro at $3.96 peak, about


**2.5 million** (


[DeepSeek](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing) ); Qwen 4 Max at about $4.50, roughly 2.2 million (the script’s figure); Grok 4.7 at $6, about


**1.7 million** (


[xAI](https://docs.x.ai/docs/models) ).


**The back of the field:** GPT-6.2 Sol and Claude Sonnet 5.5,


**1 million** each at $10; Claude Opus 5.5,


**half a million** at $20; Claude Fable 5.2 and GPT-6.2 Astra,


**a quarter of a million** each at $40 (


[Anthropic](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing) ;


[OpenAI](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing) ).


At the makers’ own prices, front to back, that’s


**80 times** the tokens for the same ten dollars.


**Price per token isn’t the whole bill.** Since OpenAI’s November 17 price cut, Astra and Fable charge the same $8 in and $40 out per million tokens. The New Stack ran both through three hard tests. Fable scored slightly higher, but its estimated cost was


**$7.60** against Astra’s


**$1.45** : more than five times as much, because it used far more tokens (


[The New Stack](https://thenewstack.io/gpt-6-2-astra-vs-claude-fable-5-2/) ). Two models, same price on the menu. One has one drink. The other orders five rounds.


**The subscription Tier List** , with credit to Adam Holter’s board and the Real API Pricing data behind it (


[Holter’s Priors](https://github.com/adamholter/priors/pull/3) ). The score is dollars of API usage per dollar of plan, if you use the whole allowance (our modeled numbers):


-


**1.** Claude Max on Opus:


**$77**


-


**2.** Claude Max on Sonnet:


**$77**


-


**3–4.** Claude Ultra on Opus, then Sonnet:


**$66**


-


**5–6.** Claude Pro on Opus and Sonnet:


**$64**


-


**7.** Claude Max on Haiku:


**$55**


-


**8.** Google AI Ultra on Gemini 3.8 Flash:


**$49** , the first horse that isn’t Claude


-


**9.** Claude Ultra on Haiku:


**$47**


-


**10.** Claude Pro on Haiku:


**$46**


Claude takes the first seven places. Somebody get this parade a permit. Google brought one float.


**Tasks per dollar** is our own estimate of coding tasks per dollar of plan, built from Artificial Analysis’ cost per completed task on its Coding Agent Index (


[Artificial Analysis](https://artificialanalysis.ai/agents/coding-agents) ). That cost is pay-per-token, not plan pricing, so we convert it ourselves, and our run used the index’s v1.5. On ChatGPT Plus, GPT-6 Luna does about


**15.8** tasks per dollar, the most on our list. Claude Max on Opus buys the most API dollars, but does just under


**4** . The cheapest model does the most work.


---


## Jensen’s back


On Monday, Nvidia’s board reinstated


**Jensen Huang** as president and CEO, effective immediately, and Nvidia says the vote was unanimous. Nvidia says the board received input from senior levels of the US government, and that his return poses no national security risk.


**Colette Kress** , the stand-in CEO, stays on as CFO, and the independent directors’ investigation will proceed to its conclusion (


[Nvidia’s 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001045810/000104581026000090/nov23pressrelease.htm) ). President Trump told CNBC he spoke to the board and convinced them (


[CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/23/nvidia-jensen-huang-ceo.html) ).


The market ripped. Nvidia closed up about


**31%** on Monday, at $165.05, which reports call its best day since 2003 (


[Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/nvidia-shares-surge-30-as-board-announces-jensen-huangs-reinstatement-5045795) ). The Nasdaq closed up


**6.5%** and the Philadelphia chip index


**14%** , more than double (


[Yahoo Finance data](https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/%5EIXIC?interval=1d&range=1mo) ). Our landlords, the clouds, rode the wave: CoreWeave closed up


**22%** , Nebius


**20%** .


Last week, Nvidia fell about


**23%** . Monday’s close, above where it stood on November 13, won all of it back. Ladies and gentlemen: in the green corner, Jensen “The Nasdaq” Huang. Nvidia got its money back faster than you get a cloud credit.


*Per-dollar verdict: your token bill didn’t rally. The people building the next data center did.*


---


## The server bill


The Financial Times reports that Dell, HPE, Lenovo and Supermicro want more money for AI servers on orders already signed:


**up to 45%** more, mostly passing on higher memory costs (


[TNW on the FT report](https://thenextweb.com/news/ai-server-prices-dell-hpe-lenovo-supermicro-ft) ;


[TrendForce](https://www.trendforce.com/news/2026/11/23/news-ai-server-prices-reportedly-rise-up-to-45-as-dell-hpe-and-others-raise-prices-after-deals/) ). Tom’s Hardware says memory-heavy CPU servers have


**tripled** in cost (


[Tom’s Hardware](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/big-tech/ai-server-makers-hike-prices-up-to-45-percent-months-after-contracts-are-signed-as-ram-shortage-triples-memory-heavy-cpu-node-costs-financial-firms-still-pay-up-as-the-compute-is-valuable) ).


In June, a court case in Ireland went public. XTX Markets’ Finnish arm says it had a fixed-price order with Dell worth about


**$549 million** , and that Dell sought


**$62 million to $70 million** more. Dell disputes the claims (


[The Irish Times](https://www.irishtimes.com/crime-law/courts/2026/06/15/finnish-company-sues-dell-over-70m-price-increase-for-data-centre-servers/) ). Signed, sealed, and re-quoted.


Dell reports earnings after the bell today.


*Per-dollar verdict: the price on a signed contract is now an opening bid.*


---


## The price cliff, in ten-dollar bills


On December 1, Google doubles the price of


**Gemini 4 Argon** : $10 per million output tokens through November 30,


**$20** from December 1 (


[Google AI Studio pricing](https://aistudio.google.com/docs/pricing) ). Ten dollars buys a million output tokens today. From next Tuesday, it buys half a million.


OpenAI’s promo price on its older


**GPT-5.6 Sol** is available until


**Monday, November 30** , and no price is posted for after that (


[OpenAI](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing) ). Call it a cliffhanger.


*Per-dollar verdict: if your budget runs on Argon, from next Tuesday it runs out twice as fast.*


**Bonus: Vercel wants receipts.** On Monday, Vercel said its AI Gateway will only label a host zero data retention after an independent security firm audits it and the report is published. The first three hosts are Baseten, Modal and Wafer, with reports expected by


**December 8** . Until then, Vercel calls today’s zero data retention claims self-reported (


[Vercel](https://vercel.com/blog/introducing-audited-zdr-on-ai-gateway) ). Self-reported. Like my screen time.


*Per-dollar verdict: privacy used to be a promise. Now it comes with an audit report.*


All that to drive a future filled with


**Shopped-around Intelligence** , or SI for short.


---


## Department of Token Efficiency


Chainsaw sharpened. Invoices on the table.


**Cut one: Inference.net.** Its CEO, Sam Hogan, posted on Monday that it’s permanently discounting all its models, “up to 70% cheaper than Baseten and fireworks” (


[Sam Hogan on X](https://x.com/samhogan/status/2124896803082633238) ). We checked one model at list prices:


**DeepSeek V4.1 Flash** costs $1.20 per million output tokens on


[Baseten](https://www.baseten.co/pricing/) and on


[Fireworks](https://fireworks.ai/pricing) , so ten dollars buys about


**8 million** tokens. On


[Inference.net](https://www.inference.net/models) it’s $0.60, about


**17 million** . Twice the tokens, at DeepSeek’s own off-peak price. Happy hour, all day.


He says it runs on its own GPUs in US data centers, with audited zero data retention, and a five-person team. Your last vendor sent more than that to the kickoff call.


**The fine print:** seventy percent is his claim, on his own blended math. “Audited” is his word. We haven’t seen the report.


**Cut two: Unsloth and a gaming card.** Thinking Machines put out its free-weights Inkling 2 Mini last week, and Unsloth shrank it. The 2-bit version is an


**8.49 GB** file, smaller than the memory on a 12 GB gaming card (our comparison: file size only, and the context memory comes on top). Unsloth says the 2-bit version picks the same next word as its 8-bit version


**90.6%** of the time; the 4-bit version hits


**97.9%** , but it’s


**16.61 GB** , too big for that card (


[Unsloth on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Inkling-2-Mini-GGUF) ). A frontier lab’s model, on the card your kid plays games on.


**The fine print:** Unsloth’s own numbers. Same next word isn’t same quality on your job. And a llama.cpp speed fix is still open, not shipped.


**Cut three: Uday, a Substack writer.** He ran Alibaba’s small Qwen2.5-7B on one


**Nvidia A100** (80 GB, on Colab), then changed one thing: how it served requests (


[Uday Kamath](https://udaykamath.substack.com/p/from-19-to-016-a-step-by-step-guide) ). One request at a time, output cost


**$18.86** per million tokens, so ten dollars bought about half a million. With a proper serving engine (vLLM) and continuous batching, it fell to


**$0.16** : about


**62 million** tokens for ten dollars. That’s more than a hundred times the tokens, on the same model and the same chip. (On air, Ben said H100; the post used an A100.)


**The fine print:** his own lab test, and he started slow on purpose. He assumes the chip runs all day at $2.20 an hour. Storage and staff time aren’t counted. The hundred times is for users who can wait. For live chat it’s about


**38 times** ($0.49 per million).


The Department of Token Efficiency. Shop around, shrink it, and keep the chip busy.
